SAVCOMMENT
This line is a comment. Comments in control files *.sav start with a percent sign % in the first column. Logically, they are attached to the following line. This means:
If the program deletes the following data line for some reason, the comment will be deleted too.
Multiple comments in sequence are not allowed, only the last comment will be attached to the next following data line.
comments at the file end without following data lines will be ignored.

BGMNassumed
VAL[i]=
VAL[i]= assigns the file(s) containing the raw pattern data. BGMN assumes patterns in free XY[E] format, in general: Leading comments starting with # will be ignored, all following lines may contain
angle 2 Theta
intensity (cps)
(optionally) esd.
If esd is omitted, it will be calculated as the square root of the intensity.
Special file formats are chosen depending from the filename suffix:
*.val files will be assumed to be in the APX file format of the firm SEIFERT FPM.
*.rd files with be assumed to be in an old PHILLIPS format. In this case, the variable STEPWIDTH may be uses to assing a non-raster stepwidht (STEPWIDTH != n*0.005)of the pattern data (e.g. PHILLIPS format in conjunction with a scanning PSD from SIEMENS).
*.rawfiles will be assumed to be in an old SIEMENS format.
*.gsafiles will be assumed in GSAS format, restricted to equidistant angular steps (both the variants STD and ESD of the GSAS data format).
Assignments must start with VAL[1]=..., the next file must be assigned with VAL[2]=... and so on. Data are not allowed to be smoothed, Kalpha stripped, background corrected or corrected in any other way. The files must contain the original measured data.
allBGMNvariables: STEPWIDTH=
BGMNassumed
STRUC[i]=
STRUC[i]= defines the structure(s) as to be refined by BGMN. Each structure must be defined in a file with the extension *.str. For more details, open a new structure in the editor and use help.
allBGMNvariables:
BGMNassumed
STRUCOUT[i]=
In contrary to STRUC[i]=, BGMN writes a result structure file to the file given by STRUCOUT[i]=. In particular, all refined parameter values are set as initial values.
allBGMNvariables: SimpleSTRUCOUT[i]=
BGMNassumed
SimpleSTRUCOUT[i]=
Generates "Simple Structure" file output. These structure files will contain no atomic positions data. Instead of, a complete list of F values depending on h k l (and iref for compatibility) will be provided.
In case you want to convert a LeBail refinement (without atomic positions) into a Simple Structure, you must provide non-zero values for density and GEWICHT in the input structure file. GEWICHT should refer to the true value as expected for quantitative analysis. E.g. for a 50:50 mixture of an internal standard and an unknown phase, you should place an assignement of the value of the internal standard's GEWICHT inside the unknown phase.
allBGMNvariables: STRUCOUT[i]=
BGMNassumed
OUTPUT=
The name of the result peak parameter file is defined by OUTPUT=.... If not given, it defaults to the SAV file name. The extension *.par will be used.
allBGMNvariables: STANDARDPAR=
BGMNassumed
VERZERR=
VERZERR= sets the geometry shape definition file, which may be constructed either by GEOMET (raytracing) or by VERZERR (measurement of standard profile lines). If not given, it may result from the entry GEQ=.... The standard extension of this file is *.ger.
In particular, this entry may hold an expression depending from zweiTheta (or THETA). In this case, only one squared lorentzian will be assumed as geometric part of the profile shape function. The value of this file gives the width parameter (=squared standard deviation) of this squared lorentzian in the THETA scale in radian. The intensity will be one, the zero point will be shifted according to EPS1...EPS4.
If not defined at all, a delta function like geometric shape function will be assumed (standard deviation=zero)
allBGMNvariables: GEQ=
BGMNassumed
GEQ=
GEQ= gives the interpolated geometric shape file, which results (in general) from a run of the MAKEGEQ program. If not given, its name defaults from the VERZERR= entry. The file name extension is *.geq
VERZERR= allBGMNvariables:
BGMNassumed
DIAGRAMM=
DIAGRAMM= must be defined if you wish to observe the iteration progress. Creates a file *.dia containing the raw data for plotting the diagram and may also be used for external plotting from other programs.
allBGMNvariables:
BGMNassumed
PROTOKOLL=
PROTOKOLL= is a logical switch. If defined as Y(es), y(es), J(a), j(a), the iteration progress will be included into the BGMN protocol. One line per step.
allBGMNvariables: LIST=
BGMNassumed
LIST=
LIST= gives the results of the BGMN run:
refined parameters
results of the GOALs
information about anisotropies
etc.
If not given, it will be written to the protocol window.
allBGMNvariables:
BGMNassumed
GOAL[i]=
GOAL[i]= defines a result value. In several cases (e.g. quantitative phase analysis) the results are not the parameters itself, but some functions of the refined parameters. By setting this function as the right side of a GOAL[i]=... assignment, the value of this function plus its random error resulting from counting statistics will be calculated.
GOAL numbers must start with one (GOAL[1]=...) and so on.
allBGMNvariables:
BGMNassumed
PARAM[i]=
PARAM[i]= defines a global refined parameter:
PARAM[i]=start_lowerlimit^upperlimit
BGMN needs for a start value start. BGMN allows the definition of hard lower (_lower) and upper (^upper) limits. Limits are static, this means they cannot be refined itself.
PARAM numbers must start with one (PARAM[1]=...) and so on.
allBGMNvariables:
EPS1
EPS1 is the zero point shift of the pattern, in general. May be refined within BGMN as a global parameter. Defines the zero point shift of one Theta in radians. Attention: Usually, the x axis of the pattern is two Theta.
allBGMNvariables: PARAM[i]=
EPS2
EPS2 is the specimen out of axis shift of the pattern (sample displacement errror). May be refined within BGMN as a global parameter.
EPS2*sin(Theta) for transmission geometry
EPS2*cos(Theta) otherwise, e.g. for BRAGG-BRENTANO geometry
gives the pattern shift in one Theta in radians. Attention: Usually, the x axis of the pattern is two Theta.
allBGMNvariables: PARAM[i]= GEOMETRY=
EPS3
EPS3 is the sample trancparency shift of the pattern. Useful in cases without exact knowledge of the sample's penetration depth. May be refined within BGMN as a global parameter.
EPS3*sin(2Theta)
gives the penetration depth shift of the pattern for one Theta in radians. Attention: Usually, the x axis of the pattern is two Theta.
allBGMNvariables: PARAM[i]= T=
EPS4
EPS4 is a first idea of a divergency shift of the pattern. Useful in cases without raytraced/learnt geometry shape function, e.g. for synchrotron data. May be refined within BGMN as a global parameter.
EPS4*cot(2Theta) for 2 Theta &less; 90 degree,
zero above 90 degree
gives the divergency shift.
allBGMNvariables: PARAM[i]=
BGMNassumed
PDBOUT[i]=
PDBOUT[i]= gives the refined atomic coordinates in the PDB (Protein Data Base) of the i-th structure as defined by STRUC[i]=. May be used for graphic representation of the refined atomic positions using RasMol (Sayle 1996). Attention: There are different versions of RasMol for UNIX and Winxx, which differ in the dependency of cartesian coordinates from lattice parameters.
allBGMNvariables: STRUC[i]=
BGMNassumed
RESOUT[i]=
RESOUT[i]= gives the refined atomic coordinates in the ShelX (*.res) format for the i-th structure as defined by STRUC[i]=.
Due to the nature of calculation within BGMN (different from other crystallographic programs) all spacegroups are reduced to No. 1 (non-centrosymmetric) or No. 2 (centrosymmetric) in this output.
allBGMNvariables: STRUC[i]=
BGMNassumed
FCFOUT[i]=
FCFOUT[i]= gives the observed and calculated structure amplitudes |F| plus phase angles for the i-th phase in ShelX format No. 5 (see Shelx97 manual). Cited from this manual:
Write h, k, l, Fo, Fc and f (phase angle in degree)... This is indented for input to some standard macromolecular FFT programs (such as W. Furey's PHASES program), thereby providing a possible route to a graphical display of the electron density.
All |F|s and the phase angles are corrected for dispersion. This means: They really are fourier coefficients of electron density maps. See ShelX manual.
This output is disabled if the i-th phase uses the "user calculated structure amplitudes" feature by defining FMult it its *.str file.
allBGMNvariables: STRUC[i]=
BGMNassumed
RU=
RU= sets the parameter count of the background polynomial manually. In general, BGMN as well as VERZERR chose this number automatically. This may fail in special cases, then try setting this value by hand.
Other methods for refining patterns with complicated background are
Using a measured pattern as a scaled background: UNT=
Using a measured pattern as an unscaled background: UNTC=
The Derivative Difference Minimization (DDM) Method: DDM=Y
allBGMNvariables: UNT= UNTC= DDM=
VERZERRassumed
RU=
RU= sets the parameter count of the background polynomial manually. In general, BGMN as well as VERZERR chose this number automatically. This may fail in special cases, then try setting this value by hand.
allVERZERRvariables:
BGMNassumed
UNTC=
UNTC= gives some predefined background diagram. For possible formats see VAL[i]. This diagramm will be added to the background polynomial. May be used, for example, in cases of known amorphous contamination of the specimen.
Other methods for refining patterns with complicated background are
Using a measured pattern as a scaled background: UNT=
User-defined degree of the background polynomial: RU=
The Derivative Difference Minimization (DDM) Method: DDM=Y
allBGMNvariables: UNT= DDM= RU= VAL[i]=
BGMNassumed
UNT=
UNT= gives some predefined background diagram. For possible formats see VAL[i]. This diagramm will be multiplied by an additionally refined positive parameter and added to the background polynomial. May be used, for example, in cases of known amorphous contamination of the specimen.
Other methods for refining patterns with complicated background are
Using a measured pattern as an unscaled background: UNTC=
User-defined degree of the background polynomial: RU=
The Derivative Difference Minimization (DDM) Method: DDM=Y
allBGMNvariables: UNTC= RU= DDM= VAL[i]=
BGMNassumed
DDM=
Modulated background intensity may correlate with the intensities of Bragg reflections and in this way cause errorneous structural parameters. In some cases, defining of a complex background by a polynomial (large RU) or using a measured diagram of the amorphous phase (UNT=... or UNTC=...) does not solve the problem or is impossible for practical reasons. To deal with such cases, the Derivative Difference Minimization (DDM) method as described at
L. A. Solovyov
Full-profile refinement by derivative difference minimization
J. Appl. Cryst. 37 (2004), pp. 743-749
http://www.geocities.com/l_solovyov/ddm.html
was enabled within BGMN. Simply give the entry
DDM=Yes
and all will be done automatically. As inherent for this method, no background is used at all (RU=0 will be set automatically). The default value is
DDM=No
allBGMNvariables: RU= UNT= UNTC=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
POL=
POL= defaults to one. Must be set in cases of secondary graphite monochromators or synchrotron data. In the case of Cu Kalpha radiation and a secondary graphite monochromator it should be set to:
pi==2*acos(0) POL=sqr(cos(26.6*pi/180))
In other cases, the monochromator's angle is different from 26.6 degree.
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: LAMBDA= SYNCHROTRON= NEUTRONS=
BGMNassumed
ONLYISO=
ONLYISO= is a logical switch. If defined as Y(es), y(es), J(a) or j(a); only the first (isotropic) part of the BGMN iteration is done. All anisotropies including preferred orientation correction models are not refined.
In special, ONLYISO may hold a numeric value. Then, the refinement will be cancelled if the relative progress is less than this value.
allBGMNvariables: ITMAX=
BGMNassumed
ITMAX=
ITMAX= is the maximum number of iteration steps, valid in any of the (maximum 4) refinement stages of BGMN.
allBGMNvariables: ONLYISO=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
WMIN=
WMIN= is the minimum angle in two Theta. All pattern points below this angle are ignored.
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: WMAX= CUT[i]=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
WMAX=
WMAX=</code is the maximum angle in two Theta. All pattern points above this angle are ignored.
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: WMIN= CUT[i]=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
CUT[i]=
CUT[i]= defines a cutoff angular range in two Theta:
CUT[i]=low:high
All pattern points inside this range are ignored. Must be start with CUT[1]=... and so on.
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: WMAX= WMIN=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
LAMBDA=
LAMBDA= may (or must) be specified for manually setting the wavelength/wavelength distribution. Specifies the combination of a *.lam and a *.ano files. The first gives the wavelength distribution as a sum of lorentzians, the second the anomalous dispersion for this wavelength. In particular, LAMBDA may specify a numeric value. Thus, the wavelength itself in Nanometers is specified. Its distribution will be assumed as a delta-function (zero width parameter). In this case, no anomalous dispersion will be defined. Additionally, my will set to zero for every phase (no brindley correction).
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: SYNCHROTRON= NEUTRONS=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
SYNCHROTRON=
SYNCHROTRON= does same as LAMBDA=. In addition, some internal behaviour is changed in assuming this pattern is a synchrotron measured one (no TubeTails, narrow lines and so on). In case you give a number, no anomalous dispersion will be defined. Additionally, my will set to zero for every phase (no brindley correction).
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: LAMBDA= NEUTRONS= TubeTails=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
NEUTRONS=
NEUTRONS= does same as LAMBDA=. In addition, some internal behaviour is changed in assuming this pattern is a neutron CW measured one (no TubeTails, narrow lines and so on). Additionally, my will set to zero for every phase (no brindley correction).
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: LAMBDA= SYNCHROTRON= TubeTails=
BGMNassumed
VERZERRassumed
STEPWIDTH=
Some of the files formats as possible for pattern input are not able to specify complicated stepwidths. Such stepwidths may, for example, result from linear position sensitive detectors (PSDs). In such case, simply specify
STEPWIDTH=0.017538
for example. This gives the step width in two Theta (the usual x-axis of the pattern) and will be used instead of the value specified in the pattern file.
allBGMNvariables: allVERZERRvariables: VAL[i]=
VERZERRassumed
VAL[i]=
VAL[i]= gives the patterns of the reference material (SRM660a emphasized). For best precision, identic angular ranges should be measured multiple times and the resulting patterns given to multiple VAL[i]. VERZERR accumulates such patterns, thereby a single, high-precision pattern will be constructed.
allVERZERRvariables: allMAKEGEQvariables: EPSILON=
VERZERRassumed
VERZERR=
The deconvoluted geometric shapes will be written to the fileas set by VERZERR=, default extension is *.ger
allVERZERRvariables: allMAKEGEQvariables:
VERZERRassumed
GSUM=
GSUM= is a logical switch. If defined as Y(es), y(es), J(a) or j(a); the intensities of the peaks in the deconvoluted pattern will be used for variable-intensity deconvoluted geometric shapes. Useful for example while using variable slit dimension etc.
allVERZERRvariables: allMAKEGEQvariables: POL= VERZERR=
VERZERRassumed
EPSILON=
EPSILON= defines the precision as to be reached. Defaults to 0.007. The larger this value, the less squared lorentzians will be used in the resulting *.ger file and the less is the computing time.
allVERZERRvariables: allMAKEGEQvariables: VERZERR=
VERZERRassumed
STANDARDPAR=
STANDARDPAR= gives the *.par file containing the natural line widths of the standard material (SRM660a emphasized).
Attention: Take care to unify all multiple reflectios. Unequal crystallographic directions giving identic 1/d should be unified to one line in this file.
allVERZERRvariables: allMAKEGEQvariables: OUTPUT=
GEOMETassumed
VERZERR=
Raytracing results will be written to the file (*.ger extension) as set by VERZERR=. The results are parametrized as sums of squared lorentzians.
allGEOMETvariables: allMAKEGEQvariables: GEQ=
GEOMETassumed
GEOMETRY=
GEOMETRY=describes the diffraction geometry. Possible values are:
REFLEXION for reflection geometry, TRANSMISSION for planar transmission geometry, CAPILLARY for capillary geometry.
If not set, the default value REFLEXION is used (common Bragg-Brentano geometry):
allGEOMETvariables: allMAKEGEQvariables:
GEOMETassumed
TubeTails=
Tube Tails and size/strain estimation Since the time of our first usage of the fundamental parameters profile model, our measurements are disturbed by so-called "tube tails". Tube tails mean: A small part of the X-rays emitted by the tube originates not inside the nominal focus, but up to 1 cm outside the focus. This means 1 mm equatorial broadening towards both sides of the optical focus. If not corrected, this tube tails may totally disturb the profile shapes calculated by fundamental parameters. See the following figure:
This figure shows tube tails of three different tubes operating with identic current/voltage as measured with a 40µm slit at sample position plus a 30µm receiving slit. All tubes were long fine focus types (12x0.04mm2 optical focus). The AEG FK61 tube was at 4500 hours life stage, the Thomson FK61/Siemens KFLCu2K tubes were new. KFLCu2K is a brand new ceramic type. Maximum intensities are 5500...7000 cps. Diffractometer was an XRD7 with 175mm radius.
Learnt profile shapes include this tube tails as part of the geometric function.
The tube tails depend on
Manufacturer
Tube type/specimen
Current/voltage
Life stage
Take-off angle of the X-rays (usually 6°)
of the tube.
TubeTails=...
simply gives a file containing the measured tube tails. You may use the same file format as for the VAL[i]= entry for measurement data input.
For explanation, we show the measurement of SRM 660 standard (LaB6) without (a) and with (b) tube tails correction for the used AEG tube:
We have measured the SRM 660 standard with two different tubes using identic slits. For demonstration of remaining errors, we give results using two different Cu Kalpha spectrae as cited from
H. Berger; X-ray Spectrom. 15 (1986) 241-243
G. Hölzer, M. Fritsch, M. Deutsch, J. Härtwig, E. Förster; Phys. Rev. A 56 (1997) 4554-4568
These are the results:
Cu Kalpha from Berger (1986)
Diffractometer: XRD3000TT Cu Kalpha from Hölzer et al. (1997)
Diffractometer: XRD3000TT Co Kalpha from ibid.
Diffractometer: URD6
Tube type AEG Rudolstadt
Without Tube Tails correction
size/nm 324(4) 496(6)
strain x106 0 0
With Tube Tails correction
size/nm 1109(51) 995(38)
strain x106 156(7) 152(7)
Tube type AEG Rudolstadt
Without Tube Tails correction
size/nm 308(4) 468(6)
strain x106 0 0
With Tube Tails correction
size/nm 884(31) 793(23)
strain x106 115(8) 105(8)
Tube type Philips
Without TT corr.
size/nm 610(10)
strain x106 0
With TT corr.
size/nm 944(34)
strain x106 96(10)
Both tables greatly illustrate the success of the tube tails correction. At our opinion, tube tails are the strongest fault of fundamental parameters profiles. Obviously, the uncertainties of different Cu Kalpha spectrae overdominate the residual error of our fundamental parameters approach. Otherwise, our measurements clearly shows the imperfectness of line profile standards. The total error of our approach, including Cu Kalpha uncertainty, is much less compared to line standard imperfectness.
Obviously, the data given by Berger (1986) are somewhat to broad compared to Hölzer et al. (1997). Data given by Hölzer et al. give comparable results for different anodes. Therefore, we recommend using the data given by Hölzer et al., which are available for Cr-, Fe-, Co- and Cu-anodes.
Using tube tails correction, one may think about using BGMN for line profile analysis (size/strain analysis).

GSUM=
GSUM= is a logical switch. If set to Y(es), y(es), J(a) or j(a); the raytracing process counts the successful and the failed ray paths separately. The ratio of successful to total ray path counts gives the total intensity GSUM, which will be marked up in the resulting *.ger file. Necessary for variable slits etc. In case some ray paths fail and GSUM is not set, GEOMET will give a warning hint.

integral(y,x,xu,xo...)
integral(y,x,xu,xo) calculates a numeric integral. integrand will be y, the integral will be carried out over x between xu and xo. For minmization of the numeric effort, an adaptive 7-point-formula will be used. The precision of the numeric integration may be set as a fifth parameter, default is 1E-13 (which will, for the fast converging 7-point formula, reach a precision near to 1E-15). Example:
integral(sin(x),x,0,acos(0))
will calculate 1.0.

cintegral(phi,yabs,yphase,x,xu,xo...)
cintegral(phy,yabs,yphase,x,xu,xo) calculates a complex numeric integral. The absolute value of the integrand will be yabs, its complex phase angle yphase. The integral will be carried out over x between xu and xo. For minmization of the numeric effort, an adaptive 7-point-formula will be used. The precision of the numeric integration may be set as a fifth parameter, default is 1E-13 (which will, for the fast converging 7-point formula, reach a precision near to 1E-15). cintegral returns the absolute value of the integral, its phase angle will be set to the variable given at first position (phi). Example:
cintegral(phi,1,90*x/acos(0),x,0,acos(0))
will calculate the square root of 2, phi will be set to 45.

gauss(A,x,b,eps,n)
gauss(A,x,b,eps,n) is a high-level standard functions for solving linear equation systems. A,x,b are placeholder for arrays, therefore only non-indexed names are allowed. gauss solves the inhomogen linear equation system
Ax=b
where A is the matrix A[1,1]...A[n,n], b is the right side b[1]...b[n] and x is the unknown solution x[1]...x[n]. eps is a limit for the pivot element, if any pivot element is smaller than eps the equation leaves unsolved and zero (false) will be returned. If the equation system has been solved and x[1]...x[n] hold the solution, 1 (true) will be returned.

cgauss(Areal,Aimag,xreal,ximag,breal,bimag,eps,n) is a high-level standard functions for solving complex linear equation systems. Areal,Aimag,xreal,ximag,breal,bimag are placeholder for arrays, therefore only non-indexed names are allowed. gauss solves the inhomogen complex linear equation system
Ax=b
A is defined by its real part Areal[1,1]...Areal[n,n] and its imaginary part Aimag[1,1]...Aimag[n,n], in equivalence the complex arrays b (right side) and x (unknown solution) are defined. eps is a limit for the pivot element, if any pivot element is smaller than eps the equation leaves unsolved and zero (false) will be returned. A function call is a name followed by a list of actual parameters in brackets () separated by commas. There are some predefined functions, in general. In addition, functions may be defined in the input file. Functions calls may become recursive. Only the actual stack depth of the BGMN program may become a run time problem for deeply nested function calls.

*[i...]
Arrays are variable names followed by a list of indices separated by commas, in brackets []. Indices may be arbitrary expressions.
* *(x...) expression:
*
Arbitrary variables may be defined by assigning a value. The first character of the name must be a letter, the following characters may be letters or decimal digits. This rule is also valid for the names of arrays and functions. Any variable may, in general, hold one of two types of values: either a double number or a string value. An expression is a special case of a string value. All programs use some variable names for program control. In addition, some variables may be predefined in special cases/positions by the program.

assignment:
Assignments are variable names (maybe indexed) followed by one ore more assignment characters = and a string. In special, the string may be a variable or an expression. In general, a single = assigns the string value of the right hand side to the left hand variable. Other behaviour may be controlled by multiple =. Some examples:
A=1
B=A
C=B
D==C
E===C
F====C
G=====C
H==(C) I==C+B
K==1
After doing the above assignments from top to bottom,
A holds the string 1
B holds the string A
C holds the string B
D holds the string B
E holds the string A
F holds the string 1
G holds the double value 1.0
H holds the double value 1.0
I holds the double value 2.0
K holds the double value 1.0
